decisions.hypothesis: H1 (geometric reach deficit): the target lies 0.2948 m from the mounted base while the chain supplies at most 0.16+0.012+0.11 = 0.282 m of tip chord under the frozen model's inextensible-centerline assumption, and passing requires chord >= 0.2848 m (0.2948 minus the 0.01 m tolerance). A constant symmetric 1 N baseline (12.5 percent of the 8 N input scale) is the cheapest legal seed that keeps both segments taut and minimally curved. Its purpose is to create the first real execution of this design, to satisfy the single independent physical evaluation that any later comparison-based design proposal requires, and to supply the execution artifact that MuJoCo-direct bounded sequence optimization needs as its source. Competing explanation H1-alt: the 0.012 connector offset is not additive to the chain or the tip entity extends past the distal segment end, in which case the bound is wrong and the shortfall is a control problem rather than geometry.
decisions.expected_observation: A control source artifact is created for this candidate from a constant ZOH schedule of 1 N on each of near_t0..2 and far_t0..2, with task_acceptance unmeasured. Because the pull is symmetric, the schedule describes a taut, minimally curved configuration rather than a steering command toward a target displaced 0.29 m in +x and reversed in -y/+z.
decisions.weakening_observation: If the seed is rejected or the returned schedule cannot be replayed, no execution is obtained and the geometry question stays open. If the measured native tip chord at a near-straight configuration substantially exceeds 0.2848 m from the base, the arclength argument is falsified and the problem is control design on the unchanged design. If native rollouts show strong asymmetry or strong gravity sag under symmetric pull, a symmetric baseline is not a near-straight configuration and its chord must not be used as a reach measurement.
decisions.interpretation: Predeclared: this baseline is a probe, not a solution attempt. A symmetric constant pull cannot steer to a target 0.29 m away and displaced in -y and +z, so a large terminal error is expected and must not be read as evidence about feasibility. Its evidential value is the measured native tip trajectory and chord scale, the physical coverage prerequisite, and the execution artifact for later native optimization. Any feasibility conclusion needs an actuated attempt (MuJoCo-direct search or the reserved single NMPC) or a measured chord above 0.2848 m. The affine capability routes are not cited here: task_capability already returned not_applicable for this task and establishes neither feasibility nor infeasibility.

decisions.hypothesis: H1 (geometric reach deficit) is being instrumented, not yet decided. The frozen target is 0.2948 m from the mounted base while the chain supplies at most 0.16+0.012+0.11 = 0.282 m of tip chord under the inextensible-centerline assumption, so passing needs chord >= 0.2848 m. This replay of the passive 1 N symmetric baseline measures the actual native tip trajectory and the chord scale of this design, thereby (a) calibrating whether the platform's own kinematics match my length accounting (is the 0.012 connector offset additive, does the tip entity reach the distal segment end), and (b) satisfying the independent physical evaluation prerequisite for any later comparison-based design proposal. A large terminal error is expected and is NOT evidence about feasibility, because a symmetric constant pull has no mechanism to steer toward a target displaced 0.29 m in +x and reversed in -y/+z. Competing explanation H1-alt: if the measured chord materially exceeds 0.2848 m, the arclength argument is falsified and the shortfall is a control problem on the unchanged design.
decisions.expected_observation: A complete 0.35 s measured execution of the 1 N symmetric baseline with per-sample world tip positions. Expected: the tip starts near the base at [0,0,0.15] and extends mostly along +x with a modest gravity sag in -z, so the terminal error against [0.29,-0.035,0.19] should be large (on the order of several centimetres, dominated by the unreached +x and the -y/+z offsets). The diagnostic quantity is the measured tip chord distance from the base at its largest value across the rollout, to be compared with the 0.282 m accounting bound and the 0.2848 m pass requirement.
decisions.weakening_observation: If the replay is rejected, terminates on numerical failure, or produces an incomplete trace, no coverage or reach evidence is gained and the geometry question stays open. If the measured tip chord reaches or exceeds 0.2848 m from the base, my length accounting is wrong and the deficit is control-side rather than geometric. If the tip tracks strongly in -y or +z under a symmetric pull, the configuration is not near-straight and its chord must not be used as a reach measurement at all.
decisions.interpretation: Predeclared: this is a measured probe of reach scale and a coverage prerequisite, not a solution attempt and not a feasibility verdict. Failure of a passive symmetric schedule cannot establish structural infeasibility, and a single execution does not establish repeatability, robustness or hardware behaviour. Only two readings are licensed: the trajectory/velocity scale of this design under a fixed open-loop schedule, and whether the measured chord is consistent with or violates the 0.282/0.2848 m accounting. An actuated attempt (MuJoCo-direct bounded sequence optimization, or the single reserved NMPC) is still required before any claim about reach capability.

decisions.hypothesis: H2 (gravity droop, not reach): the measured baseline execution shows the frozen geometry does reach a chord of about 0.2885 m from the mount, at or above the 0.2848 m that passing requires, so the 0.198 m terminal miss is attributable to the arm hanging about 0.146 m below the base plane and to an unsettled transient (tip speed rising from 0.233 to 0.542 m/s), not to an arclength deficit. Therefore a model-based closed-loop controller with terminal and holding tip-speed costs can convert the available reach into task success by lifting and steering the tip toward +z and +x and settling it. Competing explanation H2-alt: the reduced GVS prediction used by NMPC systematically under-represents gravitational sag or tendon bending authority, so the controller will predict success while the native plant still droops, producing a residual dominated by the z component with tensions pinned near their bounds. Null: NMPC fails numerically or produces an invalid/incomplete execution.
decisions.expected_observation: A complete same-candidate closed-loop NMPC execution with per-sample measured native tip positions and applied SI tensions. Under the frozen recipe (constant target reference, horizon 10, implicit_euler, terminal_weight 5.0, tracking_weight 1.0, holding and terminal tip-speed weights 0.1, tip_speed_scale 0.02 m/s, root_tolerance 1e-10, research_work_v1) the controller should compute tensions that lift the distal chain against gravity toward +z as well as extend along +x, so the measured tip should rise well above the baseline z = 0.003994 m and the z-component of terminal error should shrink far below the baseline -0.186 m. Either a pass (terminal error <= 0.01 m, holding error <= 0.01 m, holding speed <= 0.02 m/s) or a clearly localised residual is informative.
decisions.weakening_observation: If NMPC is rejected before execution, terminates on numerical failure, or returns an incomplete trace, nothing is learned about H2 and the droop explanation stays untested. If it fails with the tip again hanging near the baseline height despite tensions near their limits, then tendon bending authority against gravity is genuinely limited and the deficit is authority-side rather than control-side. If it fails mainly on holding speed while position is accurate, the binding issue is settling/settling-window behaviour, not reach or lift. If the measured chord across the full rollout turns out to be well below 0.2848 m (contradicting the single final-sample value), the geometric explanation would have to be revisited after all.
decisions.interpretation: Predeclared reading rules, superseding H1 which this Study now records as falsified by measurement (chord 0.2885 m > 0.282 m accounting bound; the 0.012 m connector offset is not additive as I assumed). Because chord >= 0.2848 m is measured at the final sample only, this is a weakening of the geometric explanation, not a proof of feasibility. (a) A pass on all three constraints is a complete task pass: I will publicly read that exact execution and SELECT its exact reference with zero extra confirmations. (b) A residual dominated by the z component with tensions pinned at bounds supports H2-alt (model/authority mismatch) and points to native-informed control (short_input_response_v1 channel response, direct PPO, or a native-optimised schedule) rather than to any structural change. (c) Numerical non-convergence, an invalid execution or an incomplete trace is inconclusive and establishes neither feasibility nor infeasibility. No hardware, real-time, robustness, global-optimality or structural-superiority claim is made from any outcome, and a model-predicted success is not acceptance until the native evaluator reports it.
